title: Proposal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion for Closed-Loop Traffic Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: Differentiable objectives (map, collision, and game-theoretic pursuit-evasion costs) with weights such as w_pursue and step size eta; adversary versus ego agent split.

control_mechanism.value: Gradient-based guidance on the decoded latent plan at inference, optionally in late reverse steps, with iterated best-response updates for adversaries and ego; no retraining. Model also conditions on scene context and marginal proposals.

base_model.value: Joint Transformer denoiser on a PCA action latent, conditioned on an instance-centric SIMPL scene encoder and per-agent proposals, with proposal-informed shifted Gaussian initialisation and DDIM sampling.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset, random subset of 200k scenarios for training; closed-loop evaluation in Waymax.

metrics.value: Collision rate, off-road rate, Wasserstein-1 realism of acceleration/jerk histograms, minADE; for adversarial guidance: ego-adversary collision, adversary off-road, minimum distance, impact speed.

controllability_evidence.value: Table III: raising w_pursue from 10 to 60 (eta 0.05 to 0.10) lifts Ego Adv Coll from 18.9 +/- 2.0 % to 47.8 +/- 3.4 %, while Adv Off-road rises 2.8 to 5.8 % and realism worsens 0.53 to 0.66.

stated_limitations.value: Guidance depends on differentiable, calibrated objectives, can degrade other fidelity metrics, adds compute and is sensitive to step size and weights. Official Waymo Sim Agents metrics not yet reported.

notes: Unguided model: collision 4.83% vs 11.70% for IDM. Language conditioning listed as future work.
